inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: These dedicated workers from the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are standing up against systemic injustice by protesting at the Presidential Palace and calling for a 24-hour strike to secure ironclad, legally binding job security. Even as the government tries to claim it has addressed their core concerns, these frontline public servants are right to refuse to back down, since true stability for education and youth services means real protections against arbitrary cuts and instability rather than empty promises. This isn't entitlement or a threat to traditions—it's a vital challenge to the long-standing structures of inequality that have left these workers vulnerable and exploited. The emphasis on personal accountability is just a tactic to sidestep the institutional reforms we desperately need to prioritize labor rights and support the communities they serve, especially the most marginalized.
